statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 7% (low) with Nasdaq-100 futures inside the CME weekend halt and no live price path available for assessment.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold because no tradable price path can form while index futures are halted until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, nine hours beyond this window. Stress is elevated on ten-year Treasury yields near a twenty-year high, roughly two-thirds odds priced for an October Fed hike, and an unresolved Strait of Hormuz after the reported U.S. rejection of Iran's seven-day proposal. Escorted crude volumes reported near pre-war levels partly offset that, and the first live evidence will arrive only at the Sunday reopen.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 7 while 20-year-high yields and an unresolved Hormuz keep Stress elevated
body: Nasdaq-100 index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, nine hours past the end of this forecast window, so all twenty-four assessed hours sit inside a closed market. That is the single most important fact for Tail: the pathological price path Tail measures requires a tradable tape, and none exists in this window. Friday's cash session closed constructively and without pathological structure. NDX finished at 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and roughly 0.5% below its 30,770.63 52-week high, while the S&P 500 added 0.51% to 7,743.41 and the Nasdaq Composite 0.48% to 27,068.72. VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87, near the low of its 14.68-15.94 daily range. The macro backdrop is the main source of Stress rather than Tail. The Federal Reserve H.15 release puts the two-year Treasury yield at 4.87%, the ten-year at 5.18% and the thirty-year at 5.47%, with the ten-year close to a twenty-year high; reporting verified this run attributes the move to sticky inflation, higher energy prices, heavy AI-related corporate issuance and the federal debt load rather than to stress, and notes the thirty-year mortgage rate at 7.45%, its highest in more than two years. Market pricing now carries roughly a two-thirds probability of a hike at the October 27-28 FOMC, with further tightening priced into December; the effective fed funds rate is 3.88%. Under the risk contract that combination compresses multiples and raises the difficulty of the environment without itself denying mean reversion, so it belongs in Stress and Confidence rather than Tail. The geopolitical picture is genuinely two-sided and is better documented than at the previous assessment. The Wall Street Journal, reported by several outlets, says Washington has rejected Iran's seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which required release of roughly 12 billion dollars in frozen funds, a waiver of oil sanctions, an end to the naval blockade and a ceasefire including Lebanon, and that renewed strikes are expected only after November's midterm elections. Early Saturday the Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting two ballistic missiles aimed at Khamis Mushait and two drones aimed at Riyadh, with no damage or casualties reported. Against that, Qatari-mediated contacts continue and are described as positive, and live updates verified this run report nearly forty million barrels of crude moved under U.S. military escort across a forty-eight-hour span, matching pre-war levels, with 122 vessels redirected since the blockade was reinstated on 14 July. Oil eased into the weekend, WTI settling at 92.41 dollars, down 2.33%, and Brent at 104.32 dollars. An unresolved waterway with escorted flows near normal volumes and a reported post-midterm strike timeline is weekend gap risk and elevated Stress, not evidence of an imminent pathological price path. The shared Finviz context read this run is partial: its futures and economic-calendar sections were unavailable, so no delayed cross-asset futures read is claimed here. Its available breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections are labelled latest-session with no source as-of and cannot establish current NQ structure; they showed six of eight megacaps and six of seven semiconductor names higher but with 1.92 and 2.02 points of dispersion, MSFT up 3.66% and QCOM up 3.97% against META down 3.33% and INTC down 3.45%, which reads as rotation rather than the persistent directional efficiency that would justify a higher Tail. Tail is therefore held in a 7-9 band across the window, with the small late-window rise representing accumulated gap risk ahead of the reopen rather than observed structure. Stress runs 47-52, easing slightly mid-window on the escorted-flow evidence and rising into Sunday as the reopen and a heavy macro week approach: Dallas Fed Manufacturing on Monday, JOLTS and consumer confidence on Tuesday, final Q2 GDP with the August PCE price index on Wednesday alongside Micron's fiscal fourth-quarter results after the close, ISM Manufacturing and jobless claims on Thursday, and September payrolls on Friday, where consensus looks for about 90,000 jobs after 162,000 in August with unemployment near 4.1%. Confidence is 81 and decays to 75 across the window. Verified current levels, official yields, oil, volatility, policy pricing, a seven-day calendar and primary-source geopolitical reporting are all in hand; what cannot be held, structurally rather than through thin research, is a live price path, and that is what caps Confidence while futures are closed. No danger window is published, because a narrow evidence-based window cannot be justified inside a market that does not trade.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment. The window opens in the back half of Friday's U.S. session, where Tail ran 18-20 with WATCH mapped at the 14:00Z hour and EA_ON from 15:00Z onward, and Stress sat in the mid-50s. After Friday's 21:00Z futures settlement Tail decayed from 12 to 7 and Stress eased from 50 into the mid-40s as the session's directional question closed out, with the mode shifting from mixed to normal and Confidence drifting from 88 down to 81 as the last live observation aged.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forecast hours falls inside the CME weekend halt, which runs until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, nine hours past the end of this window, so no hour can contain observed price-path structure. Tail is held in a 7-9 band throughout; the small rise from 04:00Z on Sunday is accumulated gap risk ahead of the reopen, not observed one-way structure, and it stays far below the 25 blocking threshold. Stress runs 47-52, easing marginally mid-window because escorted crude volumes were reported near pre-war levels, then rising into Sunday as the reopen approaches with the Hormuz question unresolved and a heavy macro week beginning Tuesday. The mode is normal while the halt dominates and turns mixed from 09:00Z on Sunday, when two-sided reopen risk becomes the defining hour-specific factor. Confidence decays from 81 to 75 purely through evidence ageing, since no live tape can refresh it. Mapped policy state remains EA_ON in every hour.
